metadata.title: Ray Dalio's Top Q2 2026 Move: State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust at a 2.93% Portfolio Impact

content.text:
This article first appeared on GuruFocus.
Bridgewater Associates founder boosts core ETF holdings while trimming tech giants Amazon and Micron
Ray Dalio (Trades, Portfolio), founder of Bridgewater Associates, recently submitted his 13F filing for the second quarter of 2026, revealing significant shifts in his portfolio. Dalio, who started Bridgewater from his two-bedroom New York apartment in 1975, has built the firm into a global macro-investment powerhouse managing over $150 billion. Known as the "Steve Jobs of Investing" for his industry-changing innovations, Dalio's principles-based approach emphasizes radical transparency and data-driven decision-making. His latest moves show a strategic rebalancing toward broad market ETFs while reducing exposure to high-flying technology stocks.
Summary of New Buys
Ray Dalio (Trades, Portfolio) added a total of 213 new stocks to his portfolio during the quarter. The most significant additions include:
-
Eversource Energy (NYSE:ES): 1,195,140 shares, accounting for 0.35% of the portfolio with a total value of $86.37 million.
-
AppLovin Corp (NASDAQ:APP): 146,602 shares, representing approximately 0.31% of the portfolio, with a total value of $75.53 million.
-
Consolidated Edison Inc (NYSE:ED): 623,641 shares, accounting for 0.28% of the portfolio and a total value of $68.99 million.
These new positions suggest Dalio is finding value in utility and technology sectors, potentially seeking defensive income plays alongside growth opportunities.
Key Position Increases
Dalio also increased stakes in 399 existing holdings, with the most notable adjustments being:
-
State Street SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (SPY): Added 955,446 shares, bringing the total to 5,320,308 shares. This represents a significant 21.89% increase in share count, a 2.93% impact on the current portfolio, with a total value of $3.97 billion.
-
iShares Core S&P 500 ETF (IVV): Added 323,202 shares, bringing the total to 3,002,286 shares. This adjustment represents a 12.06% increase in share count, with a total value of $2.25 billion.
The substantial boost in S&P 500 ETF holdings indicates Dalio's confidence in broad market performance, likely reflecting his macroeconomic outlook favoring diversified equity exposure over concentrated positions.
Summary of Sold Out Positions
Dalio completely exited 209 holdings in the second quarter of 2026, including:
-
Cisco Systems Inc (NASDAQ:CSCO): Sold all 822,892 shares, resulting in a -0.28% impact on the portfolio.
-
ASE Technology Holding Co Ltd (NYSE:ASX): Liquidated all 1,547,859 shares, causing a -0.15% impact on the portfolio.
